evidence: Plan fallback scope enumerates only: `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml`, `.github/llm-providers/openai.toml` (deleted), `docs/ci-provider-matrix.md`, `tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py`.

findings.finding: The fallback change deletes `.github/llm-providers/openai.toml` and lists its affected-file inventory as only external-integration.yml, ci-provider-matrix.md, and test_ci_provider_matrix.py. A string grep for `openai.toml` shows two referencing files omitted: `.github/workflows/structured-output-baseline.yml:43-44` has a separate `provider: openai` matrix arm whose `config_file` points at the deleted overlay, and `docs/local-dev-env.md:389` documents `openai.toml` as an available overlay. The config-file references are string paths in YAML/docs that LSP symbol tools do not surface, so the deletion inventory must be grep-derived — and it missed a second workflow that would then point at a non-existent overlay.
scenarios: `.github/workflows/structured-output-baseline.yml:44` — its `provider: openai` matrix arm's `config_file: .github/llm-providers/openai.toml` points at the deleted file; the arm loads a missing overlay and fails (the fallback intends to remove the openai arm but patches only one of two workflows carrying it).
`docs/local-dev-env.md:389` — prose `\`openai.toml\` is available the same way` becomes a dangling reference to a deleted overlay.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `.github/workflows/structured-output-baseline.yml` (drop its `provider: openai` matrix arm) and `docs/local-dev-env.md` (remove the `openai.toml` sentence) to the fallback-change scope.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record an observed check that pinned pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.9 resolves `openai-responses:gpt-5.5` to the same reasoning-model profile as `gpt-5.4` (e.g. compare `openai_model_profile('gpt-5.5')` to `openai_model_profile('gpt-5.4')`), rather than asserting the profile equality and the gpt-5.6/GPT-6 classifications as established fact.
evidence: Plan: 'The pinned `pydantic-ai-slim` 1.107.9 gives `gpt-5.5` exactly the same OpenAI profile as `gpt-5.4` ... so only the model id changes.'
Plan: 'GPT-6 models are rejected: the pinned library profiles them as non-reasoning (wrong request shape)'; '`gpt-5.6-*` is rejected: its pinned profile disagrees with upstream's current one.'

pydantic_ai.profiles.openai.openai_model_profile is import-resolvable, but symbol existence does not confirm how it maps the specific id 'gpt-5.5' (the profile is prefix/pattern-driven, so a new minor id's reasoning-vs-non-reasoning classification is a checkable behaviour, not an identity of the id string).
The plan narrates the profile-equality as a settled premise with no cited observation (no `openai_model_profile('gpt-5.5')` output, no test).
findings.finding: The plan states as established fact that pinned pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.9 'gives gpt-5.5 exactly the same OpenAI profile as gpt-5.4 (reasoning model; same sampling, encrypted-reasoning and structured-output handling), so only the model id changes' and that GPT-6 is 'profiled as non-reasoning' and gpt-5.6 'disagrees with upstream' — model-id-specific profile-mapping behaviour of the installed library that the plan records no observed check for.
scenarios: If 1.107.9 does not pattern-match 'gpt-5.5' as a reasoning model, the overlay sends the wrong request shape (sampling/encrypted-reasoning/structured-output), and the live dispatch run — the only behavioural proof — is the first place it surfaces.

evidence: Plan: "OpenAI's published catalogue (`https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/all`, read 2026-11-09) lists it active and newer than `gpt-5.4`"

A catalogue listing a model as generally active does not establish it is enabled/invocable on a specific account; the plan reconciles neither method

Evidence class: Partially-verified (model published upstream; account-surface invocability unconfirmed)
findings.finding: `gpt-5.5`'s existence/invocability is established only against OpenAI's published catalogue page (`developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/all`, 'read 2026-11-09'), not against the repository's own OPENAI_API_KEY account via `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` — the method the repo established (README lines 41-43) for the current ids and the only check that proves the account can actually invoke the model.
scenarios: `gpt-5.5` is published upstream but not yet enabled on the repo's OpenAI account; the post-merge dispatch run's openai job fails to invoke it (404/model-not-found) rather than on usage policy
The move trades one red run for another before the fallback can land
findings.suggested_fix: Add the account-side probe result (`gpt-5.5` present on the repo's OPENAI_API_KEY account via `GET /v1/models`, dated) to the evidence, mirroring the 2026-08-03 verification at .github/llm-providers/README.md:41-43, and broaden the fallback trigger to cover model-not-found as well as `invalid_prompt`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record an OBSERVED check that pinned pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.9 resolves `openai-responses:gpt-5.5` to the same reasoning-model profile as `gpt-5.4` (e.g. instantiate the model/profile under the pinned library and compare), and capture the result in the ticket or docs §"OpenAI arm model choice".
evidence: Plan: "The pinned `pydantic-ai-slim` 1.107.9 gives `gpt-5.5` exactly the same OpenAI profile as `gpt-5.4` ... so only the model id changes"

The OpenAI model profile (reasoning vs non-reasoning, request shape) is derived by the library from the model-id string, so a new id can resolve to a different profile — this is the exact mechanism the plan's GPT-6 exclusion relies on, proving the profile is id-sensitive
The pinned library is in site-packages (outside the readable repo root), so neither the plan's text nor this review records an observation of the resolved profile for `gpt-5.5`
Evidence class: Unverified (profile resolution for the new id not probed)
findings.finding: The load-bearing request-shape claim — that pinned `pydantic-ai-slim` 1.107.9 gives `gpt-5.5` 'exactly the same OpenAI profile as `gpt-5.4`' (reasoning model; same sampling, encrypted-reasoning, structured-output handling) — is asserted from knowledge, not recorded as an OBSERVED check against the pinned library. The companion exclusions (GPT-6 profiled non-reasoning; `gpt-5.6-*` profile disagrees with upstream) are likewise unobserved.
scenarios: pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.9 does not recognise `gpt-5.5` and falls back to a non-reasoning default profile, sending the wrong request shape and producing a different (possibly failing) call than `gpt-5.4`
The 'only the model id changes' assumption is false and structured-output / encrypted-reasoning handling differs
